Replaced a manual monthly reporting process with three Looker Studio dashboards covering about 5,000 to 6,000 activities a month, available to 519 local sections in 45 countries. Cleaned and consolidated multi-source data. Documented dashboard logic and data definitions for handover.

Analysed transaction and revenue data across about 25,000 corporate and co-brand card accounts (150,000+ transactions a month) with SQL. Found where co-brand usage was concentrated by region and flagged those regions for acquisition. Built monthly revenue and portfolio reporting in Excel (Power Query, PivotTables) on SQL extracts for senior management (Heads of Cards and Digital Banking, the Product team, the Deputy Managing Director of Retail and SME Banking), and automated the monthly data preparation with Power Query. Data and product point of contact for 120+ branches, answering card queries in the CRM. Context, not claimed as a result: active co-brand users grew 12% over the period.

## Projects

- [Online retail sales: SQL, Python and a KPI dashboard](https://gazish.github.io/projects/online-retail-analytics/): end-to-end analysis of the public UCI Online Retail II dataset (1,067,371 invoice lines, real data). SQL in DuckDB, KPI definitions, cohort retention, RFM segments, a revenue bridge, pandas cross-checks and an interactive dashboard. Code: https://github.com/gazish/gazish.github.io/tree/main/projects/online-retail-analytics
- [Card portfolio analysis and monthly reporting at Eastern Bank](https://gazish.github.io/projects/eastern-bank-card-reporting/): work case study (SQL, Excel).
- [Looker Studio dashboards at Erasmus Student Network](https://gazish.github.io/projects/esn-looker-studio-dashboards/): volunteer work case study (Looker Studio).
- [MSc thesis: Multi-Criteria Threat Evaluation for Local Climate Hazards](https://gazish.github.io/projects/thesis-climate-hazard-mcda/): a reusable spreadsheet-based MCDA template for screening-level prioritisation of local climate hazards over a 3 to 5 year horizon. Criteria: consequences, people affected, budget impact, frequency or likelihood, urgency, equity and social vulnerability, secondary consequences. Weights from a municipality survey, an ordinal 0 to 3 scoring rubric, alternative weight profiles and best- and worst-case rank intervals. Demonstrated on Tampere, Tartu and Malmö: extreme rainfall and heat waves were consistently among the highest-ranked hazards, while the top-ranked hazard differed by municipality.
- [Decision analysis tool](https://gazish.github.io/projects/decision-analysis-tool/): browser-based MCDA tool built for this site, with weighted sum, AHP pairwise comparison with consistency ratio, weight stability intervals and Monte Carlo rank acceptability. Uses illustrative, made-up example data.
